_note: LEVEL 2-32's DRAGON - entity `dragon.ent`, role `boss_spawn`. The third of the game's
four bosses, and the only one that CANNOT BE KILLED.
THE ROLE TABLE CALLS THIS 'a placeholder' and it is not. entity_roles.json's scenery_fx
note reads `dragon_claw.ent - part of the chapter-2 boss, which is a placeholder`. The
boss is ETHCallback_dragon (bytes 380209..383437), a claw (383726..386175), a whitelist
of bytecode across five callbacks. That is the second correction this port has made to
the role table, after `bouncer` (Roles.cpp).
IT HAS NO HIT POINTS AND NO BODY. There is no hp, no damage arm, no death arm, and the
node carries no <Body> - so nothing can hurt it and it cannot touch the player. Level
2-32 IS WON BY REACHING THE EXIT while it strafes you. Every other boss in the game is
a fight; this one is a chase.
THE LEVEL, measured from level31a.tscn: 2632 x 256 px (`max` at (2632, 256)); the
player spawns at (195, 158); the exit `door.ent` is at (2554, 144); there are no
crystals and no max_portals. The dragon starts at (-164, -84), OFF THE LEFT EDGE, and
`take_off` is at (2160, -16).
THE ONE LEVEL IN THE GAME WITH auto_camera, AND THE PORT DID NOT READ IT. level31a's
`properties` node carries metadata/auto_camera = "dragon.ent"; no other .tscn in all
128 has the key at all. Game::Game branches on it (bytes 110437..111736, ins 100-117):
a non-empty autoCamera builds AutoCameraController(name) as the level's
cameraController instead of the ordinary one. Neither this port nor the remake's
GDScript honoured it, so level31a's camera followed the PLAYER.
AutoCameraController::update (bytes 234777..234985) is three lines:
masterPos = master.GetPositionXY()            // the dragon
cameraPos = vector2(min(max(camMin.x, masterPos.x), camMax.x), 0)
SetCameraPos(cameraPos)
A HARD LOCK to the followed entity's x. No lag, no easing, and y pinned to 0.
ICameraController's constructor (234089..234234) sets camMin = (0,0) and camMax =
findCamMax(), and findCamMax (106773..107045) is SeekEntity("max").GetPositionXY() -
GetScreenSize() - which is exactly Camera::Clamp expressed for a top-left camera.
THIS IS WHY THE CLAW NEEDS NO CAMERA PASSED IN. Every number in the claw below is
measured from GetCameraPos(), and GetCameraPos() here IS the dragon's own position.
So the sim derives the camera from the boss it already owns, and Game::Tick keeps its
signature. The only outside quantity is the view's WIDTH, and the clamp it feeds does
not bite until x > 2632 - 455 = 2177 - past take_off at 2160, where the dragon has
already risen away.
GetCameraPos() IS THE TOP-LEFT CORNER, not the centre, and that was checked rather
than assumed: eth_util.angelscript's isPointInScreen subtracts it from a point and
tests the result against [0, GetScreenSize()]. Read as a centre, every margin below
would sit half a view - some 227 px - to the left of where it belongs.
view_width_px follows view.json's own note: 455 px at 16:9, and INFERRED there as
here. The layer overwrites it each tick with the window's real width.
ETHCallback_dragon, bytes 380209..383437. The first tick stamps elapsedTime = 0,
virtualPos = GetPositionXY(), takeOffPos = SeekEntity("take_off").GetPositionXY(),
tookOff = 0, and builds Follower(GetPositionXY() + (2, 0), 2000, 200).
Every tick, in this order:
previous   = virtualPos                       // read BEFORE the advance
virtualPos.x += scaledUnitsPerSecond(45)
if (previous.x > takeOffPos.x)
virtualPos.y += scaledUnitsPerSecond(-60)  // it climbs and leaves
if (!tookOff) stop boss music; playDragonTakeOffSound; KillParticleSystem;
tookOff = 1
else if (previous.y < scale(48))
virtualPos.y += scaledUnitsPerSecond(25)   // it sinks to its cruising height
drawnPos = virtualPos + (0, sin(previous.x * 0.1 / getScale()) * scale(13))
THE ONE-FRAME LAG IS REAL AND IS KEPT. Both tests read `currentVirtualPos`, which is
virtualPos as it was at the top of the tick, while the adds write the live one. The
port snapshots the same way rather than tidying it up.
THE FOLLOWER ONLY EVER FEEDS THE ANGLE. getPos() is used once, to build
dragonToChar = normalize(follower.getPos() - GetPositionXY()), and the angle is
clamp(degrees(getAngle(dragonToChar)) + 110 - 10, 340, 370). The DRAWN position comes
from virtualPos and never from the follower, so the follower's 2000 and 200 - whatever
they tune - cannot move the dragon. Its destination is the character while !tookOff
and GetPositionXY() + scale(128, 64) after.
THE ANIMATION IS PRESENTATION AND IS RECORDED, NOT BUILT. Frames 0-3 run forward over
elapsedTime 3000..3400 with the particle system on, and backwards over 500..900; the
frame is clamp(int(t / 400 * 4), 0, 3), anim_interval_ms is 400. The port's sim has no
SetFrame, and the guard condition around the backward arm reads as a three-way || in
the bytecode that this decode does not claim to have resolved - said plainly, because
it costs nothing here and would be a lie in a field that mattered.
Bytes 380209..383437, ins 626-768. The gate is THREE things:
!GameStateController::isFinished  &&  !tookOff  &&  elapsedTime > 4000
IT FIRES BEFORE IT TAKES OFF, NOT AFTER, and this decode had it the wrong way round
until the bytecode was read a second time. ins 634-637 load tookOff, NOT it, and jump
to the elapsedTime test when the negation is true; the fallthrough - tookOff set -
clears the gate. The same idiom appears twice more and agrees: the follower tracks the
player while !tookOff (ins 178-181) and the animation runs while !tookOff (531-534).
So the dragon strafes you on its way in, then climbs past take_off and stops. That is
what makes 2-32 a chase and not a duel.
LINE OF SIGHT, and it is a real gate. GetClosestContact(dragonPos -> charPos) is asked
for the closest thing on the segment, and the shot happens only if that thing
isCharacter - which (GameCharacter.angelscript, 337748..337852) reads the entity's own
`isCharacter` custom uint. So geometry between the two stops the shot.
THE PORT ASKS THAT QUESTION INSIDE OUT, and the reason is concrete rather than
stylistic. Shot::FirstBody walks box, sphere and hull colliders (Shot.cpp); the player
is a CAPSULE (Player::Spawn), so it is not in that set and FirstBody cannot ever return
it - the first cut of this module asked `closest->body == player` and the dragon never
fired once. Adding capsules to FirstBody would have made every portal shot in the game
stop on the player, which the original does not do.
Because the segment ENDS at the player, `the closest thing is the character` and
`nothing solid lies before the endpoint` are the same statement about the same world,
and the second is the one this port's primitive answers: !hit || hit.along >= 1. The
mechanism differs, the gate does not, and test_mp_dragon pins BOTH sides of it - a shot
taken with clear air between, and one refused with a floor in the way.
THE MUZZLE VECTOR IS THE ONE THING HERE THE PORT DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and it says so.
The original aims along radians(-GetAngle() - 110 + 29) as (sin, -cos) normalized,
offset scale(95) from the dragon. With GetAngle() clamped to 340..370 that pairing
comes out pointing left and slightly up - away from a player the dragon is flying
toward - which means Ethanon's SetAngle sign convention is not what a naive reading of
those two calls suggests, and nothing in the listing establishes it. Rather than ship
arithmetic whose sign is a guess, the port aims along the segment the firing gate has
ALREADY tested - dragon to player - and keeps the decoded 95 px offset. The intent is
not in doubt: the shot happens exactly when the dragon can see the player, and it is
aimed at the player. The divergence is bounded by the clamp's own 30-degree band.
The projectile is addFireball's, the carranca's own function (417483..417923):
fireball.ent with killMainCharacter set, SetGravityScale(0), playFireballSound. So it
is a Turrets::Fireball, pushed into the level's list exactly as the fire diamond's
conversion pushes one, and Turrets::Tick flies and judges it.
ETHCallback_dragon_claw, bytes 383726..386175. The claw is what makes the level a
chase: it eats the floor at the camera's left edge, and the camera is the dragon.
SIX WAYPOINTS, NOT FIVE, and the sixth is why the claw can rest. addWaypoint is called
at ins 54, 82, 107, 132, 157 and 182; the last two are identical - (0,0), 0 ms,
smoothEnd, -15 degrees. Then ins 210-216 call
setCurrentWaypoint(getNumWaypoints() - 2), parking it on index 4. Because 4 and 5
coincide, the idle pose is motionless. A five-waypoint reading would have the claw
resting mid-swing.
idx  pos        hold ms  easing           angle
0   (0, 0)       600    smoothEnd         40
1   (140, 0)     200    smoothEnd          0
2   (120, 40)    200    smoothBeginning    0
3   (100, 80)    500    smoothBeginning  -20
4   (0, 0)         0    smoothEnd        -15
5   (0, 0)         0    smoothEnd        -15
1500 ms for the swing, non-repeating.
THE SWEEP IS ON A 250 ms CLOCK. ins 267 gates the whole scan on elapsedTime > 250 and
ins 497-508 zero it afterwards, so the claw looks at the world four times a second
rather than every frame.
WHAT IT DOES TO EACH CANDIDATE, both tests against the CAMERA's x and neither against
the claw's own:
if (e.pos.x < cameraPos.x + scale(94) && waypoints.isLastFrame())
height = e.pos.y / getScale();  waypoints.reset()      // re-arm and swing
if (e.pos.x < cameraPos.x + scale(64))
DeleteEntity(e); playDemolitionSound();
AddEntity("wall_destroy.ent", e.pos, 90)               // the puff, decoration
So the 94 px line arms the swing and remembers the height to swing at; the 64 px line
destroys, every sweep, whatever the animation is doing. The claw's POSITION has no
gameplay consequence at all - which is why the port interpolates it linearly and
records smoothEnd/smoothBeginning here without applying them. smoothBeginning is not
decoded anywhere in this port (smoothEnd is sin(v * PI/2), itself inferred - see
gravitywell.json), and inventing it to move something nothing reads would be worse
than saying so.
WHERE IT IS DRAWN, for the layer:
pos = GetCameraPos() + scale(waypoint.pos + (-100, height - 72))
pos.y += sin(cameraPos.x * 0.06) * scale(13)
angle = waypoint.angle
THE FOUR-NAME WHITELIST is isDestroyableByClaw (bytes 383437..383726), an exact-match
chain of string compares. NONE of the four is in entity_roles.json, so all four are
SCENERY: plain static bodies in LevelBuilder::Built. That settles the ownership
question this port asks of every removal - a crushed platform is not a mover, not a
breakable and not a traveller, so nothing walks a list behind it - and the removal
still goes through Game's Forget funnel, as a burnt crate does. level31a places 22 of
them, counted rather than assumed.
Ethanon gathers candidates from four spatial-hash buckets around the camera; the port
walks the level's own whitelist instead. In this level that is not a simplification:
level31a is 256 px tall and the view is 256 px tall (view.json), so the bucket
neighbourhood spans the level's whole height and the x tests are the only live ones.
The equivalence is stated because it holds HERE, for that reason, and not in general.
A VICTORY CUTSCENE, AND THE PORT CLAIMS IT AS PLAYED WITHOUT BUILDING IT. Said here
plainly, because this is the one claim in this step that is not backed by a mechanism.
ETHCallback_dragon_knight_spawn (386175..386379) does nothing at all until
GameStateController::isFinished - the port's Goals::State::completed - and then adds a
dragon_knight.ent and deletes itself. The knight (386379..388631) shuttles waypoint0
(2360, 175; metadata/hold = 800) to waypoint1 (2548, 175) with a 16 px arrival radius,
and when SeekEntity finds no further waypoint it deletes itself and calls
levelFinishedEffect, which adds red_suck_effect.ent at the door. Every one of those is
after the win.
The port's layer leaves a level the tick goals.completed goes true, so none of it
could ever be seen. Dragon::Plays therefore answers true for `dragon_knight_spawn` on
the same ground `darkest` is carried rather than acted on: everything it does is
presentation. What makes the claim honest is that level31a's PLAY does not rest on it -
the level is won by walking to the exit past a dragon and a collapsing floor, and
test_mp_dragon asserts that, not the knight.
One more role-table snag, harmless but recorded: `waypoint0` is listed under the
`waypoint` role and `waypoint1` is listed nowhere, so the knight's two markers are
classified inconsistently. Neither has a gameplay consequence here.
